svg.text: Stage A, all 5 servos + OLED on the breadboards (no soldering)
Servo power comes from the kit's Power Supply Module on its own rail, never from the ESP32. The ESP32 runs from the PC's USB. Grounds joined.
Holes a-e of one row are joined; so are f-j. Each rail (+ or -) is one long strip down the board.
Jumpers (holes on the RIGHT board unless marked L):
ground join: b14 (ESP32 GND row) -> right outer - rail
rail bridge: right outer + -> L outer + (row 22)
rail bridge: right outer - -> L outer - (row 24)
signals: e7 D18 -> servo 0, e6 D19 -> servo 1, e1 D23 -> servo 2,
L f6 D32 -> servo 3, L f7 D33 -> servo 4
each servo red -> + rail, brown -> - rail next to it
OLED: GND d14, VCC d15 (3V3), SCL d2 (D22), SDA d5 (D21)
Plugs onto the bottom end of the RIGHT board: its pins in both rail pairs.
Match its printed + / - to the board's red (+) and blue (-) lines.
Outer side jumper (servo rail) on 5V. Inner side jumper on OFF.
Switch pushed IN. Check the rail with the meter before plugging servos: ~5 V.
Never feed the module from the PC's USB, never join this rail to VIN.
9 V battery: about 700 mA at most. Move 1-2 servos at a time.
C1: long leg in the + rail, striped leg in the - rail.
Unplug USB and the module's power while wiring. Plug servos one at a time, test each on the Servo control page.
